agent.builtinReadDesc: Read the content of a specific file without modifying it. Best for inspecting code, config, and logs, often after locating targets with grep/find.

agent.builtinWriteDesc: Create a new file or fully overwrite an existing file. Use for new outputs or full rewrites; file deletion is not included.
agent.builtinEditDesc: Apply patch-style, targeted edits to existing files (insert/update/remove specific sections). Best for precise fixes and incremental changes; file deletion is not included.
agent.builtinBashDesc: Run terminal commands such as build, test, lint, or scripts. Execution is still constrained by the current agent's sandbox mode and path permissions.
agent.builtinTaskDesc: Spawn a sub-agent to handle a scoped task and return results. Useful for delegation and parallel analysis.

browser.label: Browser
browser.description:
Control a browser to browse the web. Supports navigation, clicking, typing, scrolling, and screenshots.
Actions:
- start: Launch the browser (must be called before first use)
- stop: Close the browser
- navigate(url): Navigate to a URL
- snapshot: Get the current page's element tree (recommended: text format, low cost)
- screenshot: Take a screenshot of the current page (use only when visual info is needed)
- click(ref): Click the element with the [ref] number from snapshot
- type(text, ref?): Type text into an element, optionally click ref to focus first
- scroll(direction, amount?): Scroll the page, direction is up/down
- select(ref, value): Select a dropdown option
- key(key): Press a key, e.g. Enter, Escape, Tab, Control+a
- wait(timeout?, state?): Wait for the page to load
- evaluate(expression): Execute JavaScript on the page
- show: Bring the browser window to front

Important: [ref] numbers from snapshot become invalid after page changes. A new snapshot is automatically returned after each navigate/click.
browser.keyDesc: Key name (required for key), e.g. Enter, Escape, Tab, Control+a
browser.timeoutDesc: Timeout in milliseconds (optional for wait, default 5000)
browser.stateDesc: Wait state (optional for wait): domcontentloaded / idle
browser.pressEnterDesc: Press Enter after typing (optional for type)

computerUse.label: Computer Use
computerUse.description: Control local desktop applications via native GUI automation (screenshots, clicks, typing, scrolling, key combos). When enabled, it exposes mcp__computer_use__* tools for real app interactions.

claudeInChrome.label: Claude in Chrome
claudeInChrome.description: Use the signed-in Chrome browser and extension to operate real tabs. When enabled, it exposes mcp__claude_in_chrome__* tools.

minimaxMcpWebSearch.label: MiniMax Web Search

minimaxMcpUnderstandImage.label: MiniMax Image Understanding
minimaxMcpUnderstandImage.description: When enabled, exposes MiniMax MCP tool mcp__MiniMax__understand_image for remote image understanding.

describeImages.label: Describe Images
describeImages.description:
Read images and return textual descriptions.
By default it uses user-uploaded images in the current session; you can also pass absolute image paths via image_paths / image_path.
Use when the user's request depends on image content.
describeImages.imageIdsDesc: Array of image IDs to analyze (1-based). Omit to analyze all images
describeImages.imagePathsDesc: Array of absolute image paths to analyze (supports file:// URI)
describeImages.imagePathDesc: (Compat) Single absolute image path (supports file:// URI)
describeImages.promptDesc: Focus instruction for what to extract from images

generateImages.label: Generate Images
generateImages.description:
Generate images with the MiniMax image generation API.
Supports text-to-image and image-to-image:
- text-to-image: provide a prompt
- image-to-image: upload images in the current session, then set mode=image2image (or mode=auto for automatic detection)

generateImages.providerDesc: Optional provider selection: minimax or modelscope; defaults to auto-select available provider
generateImages.referenceTypeDesc: Reference type for MiniMax subject_reference.type, default is character
generateImages.countDesc: Number of images to generate, default 1, max 4

channel.label: Channel
channel.description:
Manage channel messages (for broadcasts and group discussions).
Actions:
- read(channel, count?): View recent messages in a channel
- post(channel, content): Send a message to a channel
- create(name, members, intro?): Create a new channel
- list: View channels you have joined.
channel.countDesc: Number of messages to read (optional for read, default 20)

artifact.label: Create Preview
artifact.description:
Call this tool when you need to show the user an HTML page, code snippet, or long-form Markdown content.
Content is rendered in a standalone preview panel where the user can view results in real time.
Good for: runnable HTML/CSS/JS pages, interactive visualizations, SVG charts, complete code files, long formatted documents.
Not for: short text replies, conversational answers, one-line code snippets (just show those inline).
artifact.typeDesc: Content type: html (rendered page), code (syntax highlighted), markdown (document)
artifact.titleDesc: Display title, a short description of the content
artifact.contentDesc: Full content (HTML source / code / Markdown text)
artifact.languageDesc: Programming language (only for type=code), e.g. javascript, python, css

askAgent.label: Cross-Agent Call
askAgent.description:
Assign a task to one or more agents and get immediate results. The target agents process tasks on the spot and respond, and you can relay the results to the user.
Good for: code review, translation, domain-specific analysis, or any task requiring instant feedback.
Target agents respond with their own persona and model, can use their enabled Skills, and can only use tools allowed by that agent's Tool Permissions settings.
In channel mode, pass channel so called agents post directly in that channel as themselves; when multiple agents are provided, calls run in parallel.
askAgent.agentsDesc: Optional array of target agent IDs. If provided, calls run in parallel
askAgent.taskDesc: Task description (the full prompt the other agent sees)
askAgent.channelDesc: Optional channel ID. If provided, the called agent posts directly in that channel

dm.label: Direct Message
dm.description:
Send a single direct message to another agent to inform them of something.
Do not use this tool to assign tasks or get results; that is ask_agent's job.

messageAgent.label: Message Agent
messageAgent.description:
Send a direct message to another agent and wait for a reply. Use when you need to consult or coordinate with another agent.
The other agent responds based on their own persona and config. The conversation takes place in a DM space, not through channels.
Important: Messages are sent as yourself, not on behalf of the user. For example, if the user says 'go chat with ming', write in your own voice (e.g. 'ming, how's it going?'), not 'the user wants to chat with you'.
messageAgent.maxTurnsDesc: Maximum number of back-and-forth turns, default 3. The other agent can end early with <done/>.

cron.label: Scheduled Tasks
cron.description:
Create and manage scheduled tasks. Scheduled tasks run automatically in the background, spawning an independent session to execute the specified prompt when triggered.
Actions:
- list: View all tasks
- add(type, schedule, prompt, label?, model?): Create a task
  - type "at": One-time, schedule is an ISO time string
  - type "every": Interval, schedule is milliseconds (e.g. 3600000 = 1 hour)
  - type "cron": Cron expression (e.g. "0 7 * * *" = every day at 7 AM)
  - model: Optional, specify the model for task execution (defaults to the chat model)
- remove(id): Delete a task
- toggle(id): Enable/disable a task

For add, write prompt as an execution instruction: include task goal, decision criteria, and whether to notify. If notification is needed, specify notify title/body/target clearly. Avoid slogan-like one-liner reminders only.
cron.typeDesc: Schedule type: at | every | cron (optional; inferred from schedule when omitted)
cron.scheduleDesc: Schedule parameter: at=ISO time; every=1m/5m/1h/60000; cron=5-field expression (e.g. 0 7 * * *). Do not use "every minute" with type=cron
cron.promptDesc: Execution instruction for when the task triggers (required for add). Recommend specifying: what to do, when to call notify, and notify title/body/target
cron.modelDesc: Specify execution model (optional, defaults to the chat model)

notify.label: Notification
notify.description:
Send a system notification (desktop popup) to the user.
Use cases:
- The user says 'remind me about xxx', 'notify me when...', 'don't let me forget xxx'
- A scheduled task prompt explicitly includes notification intent
- A monitoring/scheduled task discovers something requiring user attention
If everything is normal with no issues, do not call this tool.

todo.label: Todo
todo.description:
Manage a todo list within the current session. Use this tool to track progress and break down sub-tasks when performing multi-step tasks.
Actions:
- list: View all todos
- add(text): Add a todo item
- toggle(id): Toggle completion status
- clear: Clear all todos

pinnedMemory.pinDescription: Save an item to pinned memory. Use when the user says 'remember this', 'note this down', 'don't forget this later'. Pinned memories are always kept in context.
pinnedMemory.unpinDescription: Remove an item from pinned memory. Use when the user says 'forget xxx' or 'delete this memory'. Supports fuzzy matching: any line containing the keyword you provide will be removed.
pinnedMemory.unpinKeywordDesc: Keyword of the memory to remove, matched fuzzily

experience.recallDescription: Browse the experience library. Without parameters, returns an overview of all categories. With a category name, returns specific experiences in that category. When the user asks you to do a concrete task (write code, research, create documents, analyze problems, etc.), check this tool first for relevant experience before starting. Not needed for casual chat, Q&A, or everyday conversation.
experience.recallCategoryDesc: Category name. Omit to get an overview of all categories
experience.recordDescription: Record a lesson learned to the experience library. Use when: the user points out a mistake and explains the correct approach, you discover an effective method after trying multiple approaches, or the user explicitly says 'from now on do/don't do this'. Each entry should be concise and direct, one sentence.
experience.recordCategoryDesc: Category for the experience, a 2-4 word phrase, e.g. 'tool usage', 'search tips', 'response style'
experience.recordContentDesc: The specific experience content, concise and direct, one sentence

outputFile.label: Present Files
outputFile.description: After successfully creating files for the user (PDF, Word, Excel, PPT, Markdown, etc.), call this tool to present them in the conversation so the user can click to open. Only call after files have actually been written to disk; do not call if file creation failed. The first path should be the file the user most wants to see. Don't just mention file paths in text — call this tool.
outputFile.filepathsDesc: Array of absolute file paths to present to the user
outputFile.labelDesc: (Compat) File name shown to the user

delegate.label: Delegate Sub-task
delegate.description:
Delegate an independent sub-task to a background agent. The sub-task runs in an isolated context and only returns the final result, without consuming the current conversation's context.
Good for:
- Research tasks that require extensive searching and reading, summarized into a brief conclusion
- Independent sub-problems that can run in parallel with your current work
- Tasks that need simultaneous exploration in multiple directions (you can fire multiple delegate calls at once)
Not for: Operations with side effects like modifying files or executing commands

Important: The task parameter must contain complete instructions and necessary background, as the sub-task cannot see the current conversation history.
delegate.taskDesc: Full instructions for the sub-task, including necessary background
delegate.modelDesc: Specify model (optional, defaults to utility model)

claudeCore.label: Claude Core
claudeCore.description:
Delegate complex coding tasks to your local claude-core CLI. Best for refactors, multi-step debugging, and cross-file implementation.
Provide clear goals, constraints, and acceptance criteria. Use cwd to run in a specific directory when needed.
claudeCore.taskDesc: Complete task description for Claude Core
claudeCore.cwdDesc: Optional execution directory (absolute path). Defaults to current session cwd
claudeCore.modelDesc: Optional model override for Claude Core
claudeCore.continueDesc: Optional: continue previous Claude Core session (maps to -c). If omitted, auto mode is used: related task tends to continue, new task tends to start fresh.

installSkill.label: Install Skill
installSkill.description: Install a new skill for yourself. Mode A: Provide a GitHub repo URL (containing SKILL.md) to auto-fetch and install. Mode B: Directly provide skill_content + skill_name, for self-authored skills. The skill takes effect immediately after installation.
installSkill.reasonDesc: Explain why this skill is needed (for audit, required)

updateSettings.label: Settings
updateSettings.description:
Modify Hanako's settings. Two actions available:
- search + query: Search settings by keyword, see current values and options
- apply + key + value: Change a setting (requires user confirmation)

If you already know the exact key, you can apply directly.
updateSettings.actionDesc: Action: search to find settings / apply to change a setting
updateSettings.searchNoResults: No settings matching "{query}". Try a broader keyword.
updateSettings.searchMissingQuery: The search action requires a query parameter.
updateSettings.applyMissingParams: The apply action requires both key and value parameters.

sandbox.blocked:
[Security] {reason}

This operation was blocked by Hanako's sandbox security policy. This is not a bug, but a security protection mechanism at work. Please inform the user that the operation was blocked and explain the reason. Users can adjust sandbox policy in settings.
sandbox.noSu: su user switching is not allowed
sandbox.noChmod: Changing file permissions is not allowed
sandbox.noChown: Changing file ownership is not allowed
sandbox.noDelRecursive: Recursive file deletion (del /s) is not allowed
sandbox.noRmdirRecursive: Recursive directory deletion (rmdir /s) is not allowed
sandbox.noTakeown: Taking file ownership is not allowed
sandbox.noIcacls: Modifying file ACL permissions is not allowed
sandbox.noSchtasks: Creating scheduled tasks is not allowed
sandbox.noScService: Operating system services is not allowed
sandbox.noPsExecutionBypass: Bypassing PowerShell execution policy is not allowed
sandbox.noBcdedit: Modifying boot configuration is not allowed
sandbox.writeRestricted: [Security] File system writes are restricted to the workspace. This operation was blocked by sandbox security policy. Please inform the user.
sandbox.osRequired: [sandbox] Strict/Balanced mode requires OS-level sandbox, but current platform does not support it ({platform}). Please install sandbox-exec (macOS) or bubblewrap (Linux), or switch to relaxed mode (full-access).
